items.title: [Bug][CPU][Spec Decode]: --use-fp64-gumbel silently ignored in CPU recovered-token sampling (inv_q downcast to fp32); in-code comment claims otherwise
items.body:
### Summary

`--use-fp64-gumbel` promises fp64 Gumbel/exponential-race noise so that lower-tail sampling events survive (`ModelConfig.use_fp64_gumbel` docstring, `vllm/config/model.py:265-269`: "FP64 preserves lower-tail sampling events that fp32 uniform/exponential draws can truncate"). PR #43150 ("Fix FP64 Gumbel precision coverage", merged) extended the flag to spec-decode recovery sampling for exactly this reason — its description states V1 sampling and spec decode "still used fp32 exponential noise even when the precision flag was enabled".

On the CPU backend, that guarantee is silently broken: the CPU fallback for the recovered-token kernel accepts `USE_FP64_GUMBEL` and then downcasts the fp64 noise to fp32 before the argmax (`inv_q.to(torch.float32)`, `vllm/utils/cpu_triton_utils.py:451`). The comment above it claims the opposite — "the flag is accepted for interface parity and the value is read at its existing dtype" (`cpu_triton_utils.py:437-440`) — which is factually wrong given line 451. No warning is emitted; with the flag on, CPU spec-decode recovery sampling runs at exactly fp32 semantics (measured below).

Found via a systematic audit of accepted-but-unread behavioral flags; this was the one live hit out of 61 candidates.

### Reproduction (seconds; no model, no server, no GPU)

The script below calls the CPU shim directly with synthetic fp64 `inv_q`, mirroring how `sample_recovered_tokens` builds it when the flag is on (`q_dtype = torch.float64`, `inv_q = q.reciprocal()`, `vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py:681-694`; threaded as `USE_FP64_GUMBEL=use_fp64_gumbel` at `rejection_sampler.py:708`; the CPU runner monkey-patches the shim over that kernel at `vllm/v1/worker/cpu_model_runner.py:116-117`).

Observed output on a from-source CPU build at `259a209b` (`vllm 0.28.1rc1.dev259+g259a209bf.cpu`, torch 2.13.0, macOS arm64; identical results from a standalone harness compiling the unmodified `csrc/cpu/spec_decode_utils.cpp` against the unmodified shim):

```
(a) normal range                   shim(flag=on)=[1]  fp64_ref=[1]  fp32_ref=[1]  -> OK (fp64 parity)
(b1) near-tie below fp32 eps       shim(flag=on)=[0]  fp64_ref=[1]  fp32_ref=[0]  -> DIVERGES from fp64
(b2) overflow steals argmax        shim(flag=on)=[0]  fp64_ref=[1]  fp32_ref=[0]  -> DIVERGES from fp64
(b3) NaN probe (0 * inf entry)     shim(flag=on)=[2]  fp64_ref=[2]  fp32_ref=[0]  -> OK (fp64 parity)
    fp32 score at masked entry: 0.0 * inf = nan (NaN present in score vector; selected=[2], fp64_ref=[2])
(ctl) flag off                     shim(flag=off)=[0]  fp32_ref=[0]
```

Three rows carry the claim:

| Config | Recovered token | fp64 promise |
|---|---|---|
| CPU, flag **on**, fp64-resolvable near-tie (b1) | 0 | 1 |
| CPU, flag **on**, lower-tail draw `q ≈ 1e-40` (b2) | 0 | 1 |
| CPU, flag **off** (control) | 0 | n/a — matches flag-on exactly |

The flag-on and flag-off rows are identical: the flag is a no-op on this path. Case (b2) is the exact regime the flag exists for — an exponential draw below ~3e-39 gives `inv_q > 3.4e38`, which overflows to `inf` at the downcast, and a tiny-probability token steals the argmax.

The GPU Triton kernel honors the flag: `USE_FP64_GUMBEL: tl.constexpr` selects an fp64 accumulator and `inv_q` is loaded at its native dtype (`rejection_sampler.py:883, 904-907, 934-944`). So GPU and CPU produce different recovered tokens for the same random draws when the flag is on — the parity that #43150 established does not hold on CPU.

**NaN behavior (checked):** `0 × inf = NaN` scores do occur inside the kernel (arm b3), but the C++ argmax uses a strict `val > best_val` comparison (`csrc/cpu/spec_decode_utils.cpp:481-485`), which is false for NaN — so NaN entries can never be selected and never reach output tokens. The corruption is limited to wrong argmax winners (b1/b2), not NaN poisoning.

<details>
<summary>repro_use_fp64_gumbel_cpu.py</summary>

```python
import torch

import vllm._C  # noqa: F401  (registers the torch.ops._C CPU kernels)
import vllm.utils.cpu_triton_utils as cpu_tl


def cpu_shim(target_probs_f32, inv_q_f64, draft_ids, use_fp64_gumbel=True):
    """One request, N draft positions, NO_DRAFT_PROBS path."""
    ntok, vocab = target_probs_f32.shape
    out = torch.zeros(ntok, dtype=torch.int64)
    cpu_tl._sample_recovered_tokens_kernel_impl(
        out,
        torch.tensor([ntok], dtype=torch.int64),  # cu_num_draft_tokens
        draft_ids,
        None,  # draft_probs
        target_probs_f32,
        inv_q_f64,  # fp64, as rejection_sampler.py builds it when the flag is on
        vocab,
        NO_DRAFT_PROBS=True,
        USE_FP64_GUMBEL=use_fp64_gumbel,
    )
    return out


def reference(target_probs_f32, inv_q, draft_ids, dtype):
    """What the flag promises (dtype=float64) / plain fp32 semantics
    (dtype=float32). Mirrors the GPU kernel: mask draft token, score =
    prob * inv_q, argmax."""
    prob = target_probs_f32.to(dtype).clone()
    prob[torch.arange(len(draft_ids)), draft_ids] = 0.0
    score = prob * inv_q.to(dtype)  # single request: inv_q row broadcast
    return score.argmax(dim=-1)


def run_case(name, target_probs, inv_q, draft_ids):
    got = cpu_shim(target_probs, inv_q, draft_ids)
    want64 = reference(target_probs, inv_q, draft_ids, torch.float64)
    want32 = reference(target_probs, inv_q, draft_ids, torch.float32)
    verdict = "OK (fp64 parity)" if torch.equal(got, want64) else "DIVERGES from fp64"
    print(
        f"{name:34s} shim(flag=on)={got.tolist()}  "
        f"fp64_ref={want64.tolist()}  fp32_ref={want32.tolist()}  -> {verdict}"
    )
    return got, want64, want32


print(f"torch {torch.__version__}")
from importlib.metadata import version  # noqa: E402

print(f"vllm  {version('vllm')}")
print()

# --- Arm (a): normal range, well separated -> shim should match fp64 ref ---
tp = torch.tensor([[0.2, 0.7, 0.1]], dtype=torch.float32)
inv_q = torch.tensor([[3.0, 1.0, 2.0]], dtype=torch.float64)
draft = torch.tensor([2], dtype=torch.int64)
run_case("(a) normal range", tp, inv_q, draft)

# --- Arm (b1): fp64-resolvable near-tie, below fp32 resolution ---
# inv_q differs at 2^-40: fp64 argmax picks index 1; downcast collapses the
# tie and the C++ strict '>' keeps index 0.
tp = torch.tensor([[0.5, 0.5, 0.0]], dtype=torch.float32)
inv_q = torch.tensor([[1.0, 1.0 + 2.0**-40, 1.0]], dtype=torch.float64)
draft = torch.tensor([2], dtype=torch.int64)
run_case("(b1) near-tie below fp32 eps", tp, inv_q, draft)

# --- Arm (b2): lower-tail exponential draw, inv_q > fp32 max ---
# q ~ 1e-40 -> inv_q = 1e40 overflows to inf on downcast; a tiny-probability
# token then scores inf and steals the argmax from the true fp64 winner.
tp = torch.tensor([[1e-6, 0.9, 0.0]], dtype=torch.float32)
inv_q = torch.tensor([[1.0e40, 3.0e38, 1.0]], dtype=torch.float64)
draft = torch.tensor([2], dtype=torch.int64)
run_case("(b2) overflow steals argmax", tp, inv_q, draft)

# --- Arm (b3): NaN probe: prob == 0 at an overflowed inv_q entry ---
# fp32: 0 * inf = NaN. Check whether NaN can win the argmax or otherwise
# corrupt the result (C++ loop: `val > best_val` is false for NaN).
tp = torch.tensor([[0.0, 0.3, 0.7]], dtype=torch.float32)
inv_q = torch.tensor([[1.0e40, 2.0, 1.0]], dtype=torch.float64)
draft = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int64)
got, w64, _ = run_case("(b3) NaN probe (0 * inf entry)", tp, inv_q, draft)
nan_score = torch.tensor(0.0, dtype=torch.float32) * torch.tensor(
    float("inf"), dtype=torch.float32
)
print(
    f"    fp32 score at masked entry: 0.0 * inf = {nan_score.item()} "
    f"(NaN present in score vector; selected={got.tolist()}, "
    f"fp64_ref={w64.tolist()})"
)

# --- Control: flag OFF must equal fp32 reference (not a divergence) ---
tp = torch.tensor([[0.5, 0.5, 0.0]], dtype=torch.float32)
inv_q32 = torch.tensor([[1.0, 1.0 + 2.0**-40, 1.0]], dtype=torch.float64)
draft = torch.tensor([2], dtype=torch.int64)
got = cpu_shim(tp, inv_q32, draft, use_fp64_gumbel=False)
print(f"(ctl) flag off                     shim(flag=off)={got.tolist()}  "
      f"fp32_ref={reference(tp, inv_q32, draft, torch.float32).tolist()}")
```

</details>

### Mechanism and provenance

- The line: `inv_q.to(torch.float32)` (`vllm/utils/cpu_triton_utils.py:451`), forced by the C++ kernel reading `inv_q` as `float*` (`csrc/cpu/spec_decode_utils.cpp:444`).
- Introduced by 3554ada5 (#46069, "[CPU][Bugfix][Speculative Decoding] Accept USE_FP64_GUMBEL in CPU recovered-tokens sampler") — it added the accepted-but-unread kwarg and the downcast, evidently to fix a crash (unexpected-kwarg / dtype mismatch).
- The misleading comment was added separately two days later by 2396d91e (#44029, "[CPU][Spec Decode] Enable DFlash SD for CPU").
- This is git archaeology, not experimental bisection: the mechanism is a single visible line, and the two commits above are the complete history of the identifier in this file.

### What I cannot determine

- Whether real-world token divergence from this has been observed by anyone — no CPU test exercises the flag (`grep -rn use_fp64_gumbel tests/` has no CPU-path hits).
- Whether keeping the C++ kernel fp32-only was a deliberate performance decision — the commit provenance suggests crash-fix expedience, but intent is not recoverable from the diff. The false comment is a fact either way.

### Suggested fix (small, following this file's own precedent)

Sibling behavioral params in the same file that the CPU backend does not support are assert-guarded, not silently dropped: `assert not SYNTHETIC_MODE, "Synthetic acceptance not supported with CPU sampling"` (`cpu_triton_utils.py:348, 387`). `USE_FP64_GUMBEL` is the one behavioral flag in this file that is neither honored nor guarded.

Minimal change, mirroring that precedent:
1. Correct the comment at `cpu_triton_utils.py:437-440` to state what the code does, and
2. either assert-guard `USE_FP64_GUMBEL` like `SYNTHETIC_MODE`, or emit a `logger.warning_once` that the flag is unsupported on CPU and fp32 semantics apply (assert matches the file's convention; warn-once is the gentler option if CPU users currently run with the flag on).

Happy to open a PR for either variant. As a follow-up, fp64 support in `csrc/cpu/spec_decode_utils.cpp` (templating the `inv_q`/accumulator dtype in `sample_recovered_tokens_kernel_impl`) would restore actual GPU/CPU parity; I have the repro to validate it.

### Disclosure

This report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); the analysis, measurements, and repro were reviewed and run by the submitter.

items.title: [Bug]: KV offloading impossible for GLM-5.3 (DSA indexer): tail_cache block_size=4 fails the hash-alignment assertion, --mamba-cache-mode align does not reach it
items.body:
### Summary

KV offloading (`OffloadingConnector`, and by extension LMCache) cannot be enabled for
GLM-5.3-Flash because one of its KV-cache groups — the sparse-MLA indexer's **`tail_cache`** —
has `block_size=4` and cannot be aligned to the prefix-hash granularity. The assertion in
`offloading/config.py:55` rejects the whole configuration, and `--mamba-cache-mode align` does
not help because it does not reach this group.

The error message points the operator at `--enable-prefix-caching`, which is a dead end: prefix
caching is on by default and enabling it explicitly changes nothing.

### Reproduction

1× MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, vLLM `glm-release`, GLM-5.3-Flash (MXFP4), TP1,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`,
`--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
"kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"CPUOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":214748364800}}'`

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=8704.
  Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

Instrumenting `build_offloading_config` to print every group:

```
[GROUPS] tokens_per_hash=8704
[GROUPS]   UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs block_size=8704 -> tokens_per_block=8704  layers=24  first=...layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache
[GROUPS]   UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs block_size=4    -> tokens_per_block=4     layers=12  first=...layers.3.self_attn.indexer.tail_cache
[GROUPS]   MambaSpec               block_size=8704 -> tokens_per_block=8704  layers=12  first=...layers.0.self_attn
[GROUPS]   MambaSpec               block_size=8704 -> tokens_per_block=8704  layers=11  first=...layers.1.self_attn
[GROUPS]   MambaSpec               block_size=8704 -> tokens_per_block=8704  layers=11  first=...layers.2.self_attn
```

Every group aligns to 8704 except `indexer.tail_cache`.

### Why `--mamba-cache-mode align` does not fix it

It does exactly what it promises, verified by instrumenting
`Platform._align_hybrid_block_size`:

```
[ALIGN] called. mamba_cache_mode='align' block_size=8704 mamba_block_size=16
[ALIGN] set: mamba_block_size=8704
```

`mamba_block_size` goes 16 → 8704 and the MambaSpec groups follow. But `tail_cache` is not a
Mamba group — it is a small per-sequence ring buffer holding recent raw K+gate to seed the
indexer's boundary pool (see the comment in `models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py`: *"prefill
(seeds the boundary pool) and decode (per-step stash); read by the decode kernel to compress the
boundary pool"*). Nothing in the alignment path touches it, and semantically it has no
per-token block size to align.

With and without `--mamba-cache-mode align`, KV pool, timings and prefix-hit counts are
byte-identical (10,360,556 tokens; 2.25 s / 2.26 s / 0.75 s on a repeated 38k prompt), so the
flag is a no-op for this model apart from the mamba block size itself.

### Why this matters

Prefix caching on the GPU works well here — measured with a unique needle mid-context, hits read
from `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` (the API does not report `cached_tokens`):

| context | prefix hits from run 2 | share | needle |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 000 | 147 968 → 513 536 | | 5/5 verbatim |
| 200 000 | 156 672 | 78 % | 5/5 verbatim |
| 600 000 | 478 720 | 80 % | 5/5 verbatim |

But it is bounded by GPU memory. The capacity argument for offloading is strong on this box:

| tier | capacity | 1M-token contexts |
|---|---|---|
| GPU (8 × 11.2M tokens) | 89.8M | 87 |
| host RAM (2 055 GB free) | 282M | 272 |
| disk (1.4 TB free) | 192M | 185 |

and a miss at 1M context costs **95.0 s** of prefill (measured, TP1) versus roughly 0.3 s to move
6.92 GB back over PCIe. That is the difference offloading would buy on long-context workloads.

### Suggested directions

1. **Let groups whose block size is smaller than `tokens_per_hash` opt out of offloading**
   rather than failing the whole configuration — but only if such a group can be *recomputed*
   rather than restored. For `tail_cache` that needs a maintainer's judgement: if the tail is not
   restored alongside the offloaded KV, the indexer's boundary pool is seeded from stale state
   and attention is silently wrong. **A blanket skip would trade a startup error for silent
   corruption, which is why I did not patch around it locally.**
2. **Fix the error message.** "need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes" sends the
   operator down a dead end when prefix caching is already enabled — which is the default. It
   would help to name the offending group and its layers.
3. If `tail_cache` genuinely cannot participate, it would be worth stating in the docs that
   KV offloading (and LMCache) is unavailable for DSA-indexer models, so operators do not spend
   time on it.

Happy to test a patch on this hardware — the setup above reproduces in one start.

items.title: [Feature][Frontend] Add reasoning and content phase per-request metrics
items.body:
## Summary

Add per-request token and timing metrics that distinguish reasoning generation from final content generation for reasoning models.

This issue is intentionally separate from #54828. That issue adds the existing overall per-request timing metrics to `/v1/responses`; this issue introduces new phase-aware accounting and timing semantics.

## Motivation

For reasoning models, aggregate output metrics combine two operationally different phases:

1. Internal reasoning generation.
2. Final content generation returned to the caller.

Production users need to attribute token usage and latency to those phases independently, including:

- Reasoning token count versus final-content token count.
- Time to first reasoning token.
- Time to first content token.
- Generation time for each phase.
- Inter-token latency and throughput for each phase.

The existing overall TTFT is normally the time to the first reasoning token. It does not report how long the caller waits for the first final-content token.

## Existing behavior

The OpenAI-compatible usage objects can report reasoning-token counts:

- Responses: `usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`
- Chat Completions: `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`

#45802 provides token-aware reasoning counting through the reasoning parser.

#46768 provides overall per-request timing metrics for Chat Completions and Completions, but explicitly identifies reasoning-versus-final-answer metrics as future work.

No current response reports phase-specific TTFT, generation time, ITL, or throughput.

## Proposed behavior

Extend the existing optional `metrics` object with phase-specific metrics while preserving the current overall fields.

One possible shape is:

```json
{
  "metrics": {
    "time_to_first_token_ms": 108.22,
    "generation_time_ms": 420.0,
    "queue_time_ms": 12.3,
    "mean_itl_ms": 7.5,
    "tokens_per_second": 110.0,
    "reasoning": {
      "token_count": 36,
      "time_to_first_token_ms": 108.22,
      "generation_time_ms": 160.0,
      "mean_itl_ms": 4.57,
      "tokens_per_second": 218.75
    },
    "content": {
      "token_count": 20,
      "time_to_first_token_ms": 268.22,
      "generation_time_ms": 210.0,
      "mean_itl_ms": 11.05,
      "tokens_per_second": 90.5
    }
  }
}
```

The exact schema is open to maintainer feedback.

## Endpoint scope

Required:

- `/v1/responses`, after or together with #54828.

Desired parity:

- `/v1/chat/completions`, using the same internal collector and endpoint-appropriate usage fields.

Out of scope:

- Reasoning-specific metrics for legacy `/v1/completions`.

## Implementation considerations

- Reuse reasoning-parser token classification; do not reparse the final text.
- Correlate generated token IDs or token batches with engine/frontend timestamps.
- Preserve the existing overall metrics and their definitions.
- Define a common timestamp origin for reasoning and content TTFT.
- Define phase generation time, ITL, and throughput formulas explicitly.
- If speculative decoding emits multiple tokens in one engine batch, document or avoid any precision assumptions that per-token timestamps cannot support.
- Aggregate multiple reasoning/content segments initially; per-segment arrays can be future work.
- Distinguish unsupported/unclassified reasoning from a valid zero-reasoning-token result.
- For streaming, report completed phase metrics in the final usage/response event.
- Preserve behavior when per-request metrics or server-side stats are disabled.

## Token accounting

Reasoning-token counts should remain in the standard endpoint-specific usage fields. An exact content-token count must account for possible tool/control output tokens rather than always assuming:

```text
content_tokens = total_output_tokens - reasoning_tokens
```

If the implementation cannot classify all output tokens, unknown or unclassified tokens should not silently be counted as content.

## Non-goals

- Adding separate reasoning and content token limits.
- Inferring a `reasoning_token_limit_reached` flag without an explicit engine end reason.
- Changing `max_output_tokens` semantics.
- Prometheus aggregation changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- Correct reasoning and content counts for supported reasoning parsers.
- Separate first-token timing for reasoning and content.
- Separate phase generation time and ITL/throughput where attribution is reliable.
- Streaming and non-streaming coverage.
- Non-reasoning model coverage.
- Reasoning parser absent/unsupported coverage.
- Single-token and zero-token phase coverage.
- Clear documentation of formulas and unavailable/null behavior.
- No change to existing overall metric values.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- #46768 provides only aggregate timing and lists this breakdown as future work.
- #45802 provides reasoning-token counts, not phase-specific timing.
- #54828 tracks Responses API parity for existing aggregate metrics and intentionally excludes reasoning-aware metrics.
- #42198 is a response-header proposal and cannot carry final streaming metrics in headers.

## Related work

- #54828
- #46768
- #45802
- #40076
- #42198
- #36383

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues and pull requests for reasoning-aware per-request timing metrics.

items.title: [Bug]: qwen3_coder / qwen3_xml parser silently ignores tool_choice "required" and named function on /v1/chat/completions (0.28.0)
items.body:
### Summary

With `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` (or `qwen3_xml`, which maps to the same class), `tool_choice: "required"` and a named function `tool_choice` are not enforced on `/v1/chat/completions`. The request succeeds and the model behaves as if `tool_choice` were `"auto"`. Adding `"strict": true` to the tool does not change this.

This looks like the same root cause reported for gemma4 in #50477, poolside_v1 in #49712 and step3p5 in #51804, so it is not model specific. Filing separately because Qwen3 parsers are not mentioned in those threads.

### Environment

- vLLM 0.28.0 (PyPI wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu132, transformers 5.16.1, flashinfer-python 0.6.16.post3, xgrammar 0.2.3
- Python 3.12.14, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), driver 580.105.08, single GPU
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (bf16), architecture Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
- Flags: `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 262144`
- `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING` left at default (True)
- Same behavior with the `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38` Docker image

### Repro

Tools used in all requests:

```json
"tools": [
  {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "description": "Get current weather for a city",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}},
  {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time", "description": "Get current local time for a city",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}
]
```

All requests use `temperature: 0` and `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`. Results are the same with thinking enabled.

1. `tool_choice: "required"`, user message `Hi there!`

```json
{"finish_reason": "tool_calls", "message": {"content": "Hello! How can I help you today?", "tool_calls": null}}
```

No tool call was made, but `finish_reason` says `tool_calls`.

2. Same request with `"strict": true` on the tool and `max_tokens: 6`

```json
{"finish_reason": "length", "content": "Hello! How can I help", "tool_calls": null, "token_ids": [9419, 0, 2500, 628, 353, 1438]}
```

The very first generated token is prose, so no grammar was active.

3. Named function `tool_choice: {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time"}}`, user message `What is the weather in Paris?`

```json
{"finish_reason": "stop", "message": {"content": "", "tool_calls": [{"function": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\": \"Paris\"}"}}]}}
```

A different function than the one requested was called, and `finish_reason` is `stop`.

4. `tool_choice: "auto"` works as expected (single and parallel calls, streaming included). `response_format: {"type": "json_schema", ...}` also works, so structured output itself is functional on this setup.

The same three cases give the same results on `/v1/responses`.

### Expected

`required` should produce at least one tool call, a named function should produce a call to that function, or the server should return an error. A 200 with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` and `tool_calls: null` is the worst of the options because clients treat it as a successful tool turn.

### Where the grammar gets lost (0.28.0)

Edited after more digging. An earlier version of this section said `adjust_request` is not called on the chat completions path. That was wrong: `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py` does call `parser(...).adjust_request(request)` whenever `tool_choice != "none"` or a reasoning parser is configured. The grammar is lost inside the parser, not before it.

What I verified:

- The grammar itself is fine. `get_model_structural_tag(model="qwen_3_coder", tools=..., tool_choice="required", reasoning=False)` returns a `tags_with_separator` structural tag with `at_least_one: true`; for a named function it returns a single `tag`. If I put that exact structural tag into the request as `structured_outputs: {"structural_tag": ...}` together with `tools` and `tool_choice: "required"`, the server enforces it: the model emits `<tool_call>` XML, the parser extracts `get_weather({"city": "New York"})` and `finish_reason` is `tool_calls`. So the engine and xgrammar side works end to end.

- The parser used on the request path never attaches that grammar. `ParserManager.get_parser(tool_parser_name="qwen3_coder", reasoning_parser_name="qwen3", ...)` returns `Qwen3Parser`, whose `tool_parser_cls` is the generated `Qwen3ParserToolAdapter`. Running that parser's `adjust_request` offline on a `ChatCompletionRequest` with `tool_choice="required"` or a named function leaves `request.structured_outputs` as `None`, so `to_sampling_params()` produces no structured output constraint.

- Two things make that happen. `Qwen3ParserToolAdapter` has `structural_tag_model = None` and `supports_required_and_named = True` (class attributes checked at runtime), so `AbstractParser._apply_structural_tag` returns early. The `structural_tag_model = "qwen_3_coder"` and `supports_required_and_named = False` that are declared on `Qwen3EngineToolParser` (the class registered under the `qwen3_coder` and `qwen3_xml` names) are not on the adapter class that the request path instantiates. And `ParserEngineToolAdapter.adjust_request` (`vllm/parser/engine/adapters.py`) only forwards to `ParserEngine.adjust_request`, which sets `request.skip_special_tokens = False` and returns; it does not call `ToolParser.adjust_request`, so the JSON schema fallback for required/named (`get_json_schema_from_tools`) never runs either. Net effect: no grammar of either kind is attached for required or named tool_choice.

- Setting `structural_tag_model` and `supports_required_and_named` on `Qwen3ParserToolAdapter` alone does not fix it (tested offline, `structured_outputs` stays `None`), so the missing piece is in the parser engine's `adjust_request` path rather than just the class attributes.

Given that the explicit `structured_outputs.structural_tag` request works today, the fix looks like making the engine-based parser path build and attach the same structural tag that `get_model_structural_tag` already produces for `required` and named tool_choice.

Happy to test a patch. The three requests above are enough to reproduce, and the explicit structural tag request above is a working reference for the expected behavior.

items.title: [Bug][XPU] inductor-compiled decode pieces x speculative decode livelock both GPUs at >=32k ctx (graph capture alone clean; native stacks included)
items.body:
## Summary

With torch inductor compilation active for decode (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` piecewise path) **combined with speculative decoding (MTP)**, both TP workers livelock permanently-ish at >=32k context: both GPUs show Compute Engines 100% + Copy Engines 100% (local spin, ~80 GB/s HBM, PCIe ~33 MB/s), host ranks park at the next device sync, and the engine stops serving. Whole-step XPU graph capture with eager kernels (`TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1`) is fully clean through the same battery — the defect is the inductor-compiled region x spec decode, not XPU graph capture itself.

## Environment

- vLLM 0.21.1.dev0+gad7125a43 (XPU build) + vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.8.3.dev0+g3cab97a
- torch 2.11.0+xpu, oneAPI 2025.3.2 / oneCCL 2021.15, NEO 37833, kernel 6.17.0-1010-intel
- 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 (BMG G31), TP=2
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B fp8 (GDN hybrid attention + MTP), `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc`, `--block-size 512`, `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` (k=4 also reproduces the livelock but has a separate corruption bug, see #54785)

## Reproduction

Boot with the above flags; the compile+capture+spec posture is the wedging one (in our tree a fail-safe gate disables it; we use `VLLM_XPU_ALLOW_UNSAFE_SPEC_TP_GRAPH=1` to restore it for diagnosis). Then send **6 concurrent requests each with ~65k-token prompts and DIFFERENT prefixes** (cold prefills — prefix-cache-warm requests and single streams do not trigger it reliably). Within the first decode chunks both workers wedge: ttft climbs to ~200s, both GPUs spin.

## Discriminator matrix (each row a dedicated boot, same 65k battery)

| configuration | verdict |
|---|---|
| compile + capture + spec | WEDGE at 1st 65k chunk |
| + GDN ops split out of capture | wedges (already split by default) |
| + `moe_ops::moe_forward_full_fp8_block` split | wedges |
| + ALL custom ops split (`custom_esimd_kernels_vllm::*`, `_xpu_C::fp8_gemm*`) | wedges — every custom kernel exonerated |
| compile, no capture | WEDGE at chunk ~563 (slow onset) |
| **capture, NO compile (`TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1`)** | **fully clean** (6/6 + 3/3 @65k + 10/10 canonical) |
| fully eager | clean |

Capture accelerates onset ~500x; it is an accelerator, not a necessary ingredient.

## Native stacks at the live wedge (gdb attached mid-stall)

Both TP workers' main threads parked **identically**:

```
#11 torch::jit::invokeOperatorFromPython(...)
#10 c10::Dispatcher::callBoxed(...)
#8  gdn_attention(...)                          [vllm_xpu_kernels/_xpu_C.abi3.so]
#7  gdn::chunk_gated_delta_rule_impl_xe2(...)   [vllm_xpu_kernels/libgdn_attn_kernels_xe_2.so]
#6  sycl::_V1::detail::queue_impl::wait(...)    [libsycl.so.8]
#2  v2::ur_queue_immediate_in_order_t::queueFinish()  [libur_adapter_level_zero_v2.so.0]
#1  ?? ()                                       [libze_intel_gpu.so.1]
#0  ?? ()                                       [libc]
```

The host is blocked in the **eager** GDN kernel's `q.wait()` on an **in-order** Level-Zero queue — i.e. work enqueued ahead of it on the same stream never retires while the device spins. Since the GDN kernel (and every other custom kernel) is exonerated by the split arms and capture-no-compile is clean, the never-retiring work is the inductor-compiled decode region sharing that stream. oneCCL is also exonerated (76,414/76,414 perfect eager all_reduce begin/end pairing per rank at a wedge; version-independent across 2021.15/2021.17.2).

## Workaround

`TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1` with XPU graph capture left enabled: whole-step capture with eager kernels is clean through the full 65k battery and ~79% faster than fully-eager. We ship that as a fail-safe gate for spec+TP>1 in our image.

## Related

- #54785 — separate k=4 corruption under capture (compile-independent)
- oneCCL #212/#215 — our chase originally looked like their IPC-handle/allreduce hangs; cross-posted there as a triage datapoint (our case was NOT oneCCL)

items.title: [Bug][XPU] XPU graph capture + MTP num_speculative_tokens=4 produce non-deterministic, wrong logits at temperature=0 (k<=3 clean, eager clean, bs>=2 eager fallback clean, compile-independent)
items.body:
## Environment

- vLLM 0.21.1.dev0+gad7125a43 (XPU build) + vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.8.3.dev0+g3cab97a
- torch 2.11.0+xpu, triton-xpu 3.7.0, oneAPI 2025.3.2 / oneCCL 2021.15
- 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage BMG G31, 8086:e223), NEO 37833, kernel 6.17.0-1010-intel
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B fp8 (GDN hybrid attention + MTP drafter heads), TP=2, `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc`, `--block-size 512`, `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`, default XPU capture sizes (<=128), `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":4}'`

## Minimal repro (3 curls after one boot)

Boot the server (flags above), then send the SAME request 8x at temperature 0:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"MODEL","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":6,"temperature":0,"logprobs":5}' \
    | python3 -c 'import sys,json; ch=json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0];
       top=sorted(((float(v),k) for k,v in (ch["logprobs"]["top_logprobs"][0] or {}).items()), reverse=True)[:2];
       print(repr(ch["text"]), ["%s:%.3f"%(k,v) for v,k in top])'
done
```

With k=4: outputs cycle between 2-3 variants (distinct >= 2); the top-1 logprob for the same position swings up to ~1.5 nats (-0.099 / -0.294 / -1.598 observed) and the top token itself can flip (' Paris' -> 'The'). After ~40 requests on the same boot, outputs degenerate (' France France France...').

Restart the SAME server with `num_speculative_tokens` = 3 (or 1, or 2): distinct = 1, top-1 logprob -0.451 bit-stable, all runs. That contrast is the whole bug report.

## What we established (each point from a dedicated boot/arm)

1. **The boundary is exactly k=4.** k=1/2/3 + graphs: distinct=1, top-1 -0.451 bit-stable, identical to the compile-no-capture reference (-0.453). k=4: corrupt. Not a gradient — a cliff.
2. **Capture is necessary.** `VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=0` + k=4 = deterministic (that is our reference number).
3. **Batch-size fallback is clean.** 2 concurrent requests on a capture-sizes-[1,2,4,8] boot (rows exceed the list -> eager fallback) both return the reference continuation. Corruption lives in the captured bs=1 pieces.
4. **Padding is NOT the trigger.** k=1 bs=3 (6 rows -> padded 8-piece) and k=2 bs=1 (3 rows -> padded 4-piece) are clean. The boundary tracks the draft-token count, not padded shape.
5. **Byte-reproducible.** Same responses in the same order across boots, across two image generations, and across capture lists [1..128] vs [1,2,4,8] — a deterministic function of request ordinal. The scheduler alternates among 2-3 execution paths and at least one computes wrong logits.
6. **temperature=0 IS honored**: a high-margin 40-token prompt returns 6/6 identical text even on a corrupt boot — the logits differ prompt-sensitively; this is not a sampler fault.
7. **Not a recent regression**: reproduces byte-for-byte on builds dating back ~4 image generations (>= v24-era, vLLM 0.21.1.dev line). Earlier "bare prompts are stable" observations were small-sample artifacts of the per-request-ordinal path cycling (a same-path run of 4 is unremarkable).
8. **Captured collectives are not required**: we do NOT run `VLLM_XPU_ALLOW_COMM_IN_GRAPH` (that mode returns deterministic garbage outright and is disabled); the corruption occurs with the default comm-outside-graph placement.
9. **Capture-level and COMPILE-INDEPENDENT (2026-09-01 discriminator)**: with `TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1` and whole-step XPU graph capture still on (dynamo/inductor never engage — pure eager kernels inside the captured step), k=4 STILL corrupts: distinct=3 across 8 identical requests, top-1 logprob drifting (-1.668 / -0.187 / -0.050 at the same position), no wedge through the full 65k battery. k<=3 under the identical posture is bit-stable == eager reference. This rules the inductor-compiled pieces OUT of this bug (in contrast to the separate 65k livelock we chased on the same stack, which WAS convicted to inductor x spec) and pins the defect to the capture/replay of multi-draft-position spec state.
10. **Deployed mitigation**: we clamp `num_speculative_tokens` 4 -> 3 with a boot warning whenever any graph capture is active and a speculative config is present (escape hatch env for repro: `VLLM_XPU_ALLOW_K4_CAPTURE=1`). k=3 retains most of the MTP speedup at bs=1 for us.

## Suspect area

Multi-draft-position spec machinery under graph capture/replay (capture-level, not inductor — see datapoint 9) — the same machinery as the GDN spec-kernel ragged-batch OOB we previously found and fixed locally (wheel rebuild): GDN speculative state buffers and/or the verify mask for 4 draft positions, as replayed inside FULL_DECODE_ONLY pieces. k<=3 clean / k=4 corrupt / bs>=2-eager clean / padding-refuted together point at state that is sized or advanced per draft position and not correctly reset or re-bound between piece replays.

## Impact

Any XPU user running MTP k=4 with graphs (the shipped default combination for our config) gets silently wrong greedy outputs. Throughput/stability testing does not catch it — every historical arm of ours measured wedges and token rates only, and all of those k=4 arms almost certainly served corrupt text.

## Related

- #26963 (speculative decoding support on XPU — tracking issue)

items.title: [Bug]: KDA/gated-delta-rule chunked-scan buffers are outside memory profiling — runtime OOM at large --max-num-batched-tokens
items.body:
### Summary

The chunked-scan buffers in the gated-delta-rule (KDA) path scale linearly with
`--max-num-batched-tokens`, are allocated transiently inside the forward pass, and are **not
covered by vLLM's startup memory profiling**. The KV cache is therefore sized as if that memory
were free, and above a certain chunk size the engine dies at runtime — mid-request, after having
served traffic.

### Observed

GLM-5.3-Flash (45 layers: 34 KDA linear-attention + 11 sparse MLA), 1× MI350X (gfx950),
ROCm 7.2.3, TP1, MXFP4 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`.
16 concurrent requests of ~38k tokens each.

| `--max-num-batched-tokens` | successful | failed | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 192 … 65 536 | 16 / 16 | 0 | stable across 3 runs each |
| **81 920** | **5 / 16** | **11** | engine shut down |
| **131 072** | **4 / 16** | 12 | engine shut down |

```
(Worker) ERROR  File ".../flash_linear_attention/ops/chunk_delta_h.py", line 357,
                  in chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h
(Worker) ERROR    v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None
(Worker) ERROR  torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB.
                  GPU 0 has a total capacity of 287.98 GiB of which 0 [bytes is free]
(APIServer) INFO [shutdown] EngineCore process manager: using 15.0s ROCm cleanup grace
                  after immediate request abort
```

Startup reported no problem — `GPU KV cache size: 6,940,947 tokens` at 81,920, and the memory
profiling line looked healthy.

### Mechanism

`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` allocates two buffers proportional to the token count in the batch:

```python
B, T, Hg, K, V = *k.shape, u.shape[-1]
H  = u.shape[-2]
BT = chunk_size                      # FLA_CHUNK_SIZE = 64, hard-coded in ops/utils.py:31
...
N, NT = len(cu_seqlens) - 1, len(chunk_indices)
h     = k.new_empty(B, NT, H, V, K)          # NT = ceil(T / 64)  -> linear in T
v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None   # linear in T
```

For this model (`linear_attn_config`: 64 heads, head_dim 128) at T = 81,920 with BT = 64:

```
NT     = 1280
h      = 1280 · 64 · 128 · 128 · 2 B  ≈ 2.5 GiB
v_new  = 81920 · 64 · 128 · 2 B       ≈ 1.25 GiB   <- the allocation that failed
```

That is ~3.75 GiB transient **per KDA layer invocation**, and there are 34 KDA layers per forward
pass. They are freed between layers, so the caching allocator mostly reuses the blocks — but the
peak is real, and it is not what the profiling run measured. Measured peaks from vLLM's own log,
same model, same everything but the chunk size:

```
chunk  8 192:  14.52 GiB peak activation   KV 9,578,037 tokens
chunk 65 536:  22.73 GiB peak activation   KV 7,512,186 tokens
```

The KV pool shrinks ~35 KV-tokens per extra chunk token, linearly, which is the profiler
*partially* accounting for this. But at 131,072 the loss jumps to ~60 KV-tokens per chunk token —
non-linear — and at 81,920 the runtime allocation no longer fits.

### Why it matters beyond this model

The failure mode is the bad one: **it does not fail at startup, it fails under load.** A
configuration passes a smoke test, serves requests, then the engine dies with requests in flight.
And it is silent in the metrics — `vllm bench serve` computes `Total input tokens` over
*successful* requests only, so throughput per second goes **up** as requests die. In my own sweep
81,920 initially looked like the fastest setting (+21 % over baseline) purely because 11 of 16
requests never completed.

Any model with gated-delta-rule / linear-attention layers goes through this path (GLM-5.x hybrid,
Qwen3-Next GDN, and others).

### Suggested directions

1. **Include the KDA path in the memory profiling run** at the configured
   `max_num_batched_tokens`, with a batch composition representative of chunked prefill
   (several sequences, not one), so the peak is measured rather than partly inferred.
2. **Or bound the buffers**: `FLA_CHUNK_SIZE` is a module-level constant
   (`third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/utils.py:31`). Making it configurable would let
   operators trade chunk-scan parallelism for memory — `BT = 128` halves `h`. `BT` is already a
   free `tl.constexpr` in the kernels (the `64` in the block pointers is the head-dim blocking,
   not the time chunk), so this looks mechanically possible, though I have not yet measured
   whether 128 is correct and faster.
3. **Or refuse the configuration at startup** rather than at runtime, if the peak can be
   computed analytically from `max_num_batched_tokens`, the head count and `FLA_CHUNK_SIZE`.

Happy to test a patch on this hardware.

**Unrelated but adjacent, in case it helps someone sizing a config:** the ~11.7 GiB left unused by
`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93` on a 288 GiB part is *not* free headroom — it is where these
transient allocations land. vLLM's own log suggests `--kv-cache-memory=<the full amount>` to
"fully utilize gpu memory"; taking that suggestion at a large chunk size is what removes the room
this path needs.

items.title: [RFC]: The dynamic-SD K decision is a batch-keyed array index — agreeing on its shape before more signals arrive
items.body:
### Motivation.

On current `main` (`504bb8b0c3`) the dynamic-SD K decision is one array index:

```python
# vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:1321-1324
if self.dynamic_sd_lookup is not None and len(num_scheduled_tokens) > 0:
    num_spec_tokens_to_schedule = self.dynamic_sd_lookup[
        len(num_scheduled_tokens)
    ]
```

The key is batch size, and that choice is fixed in four places, not one:

- `validate_and_normalize_dynamic_sd_schedule` unpacks entries as
  `(range_start, range_end, num_speculative_tokens)` (`dynamic/utils.py:37`)
- `build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup` returns `list[int]`, a dense
  `batch_size -> K` table (`dynamic/utils.py:77-81`)
- the scheduler indexes it by `len(num_scheduled_tokens)` (`sched/scheduler.py:1322`)
- since #50488, two capture-planning sites read the same dense table
  (`worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:219`, `config/vllm.py:2067`)

The decision site is not short of information — `schedule()` has the request set
in hand, so per-request `num_computed_tokens`, acceptance history and queue
depth are all in scope. They are simply not read. Whatever a proposal wants K to
depend on, it currently has to widen that tuple everywhere, or bypass the
schedule entirely.

**Six different signals are being proposed for this one decision right now.**
Batch size is what ships. Beyond it:

| signal | where |
|---|---|
| context length | #48944 (mine), widening the tuple to `(bs, ctx) -> K` |
| token entropy | #54082, gating K between 0 and K at runtime |
| marginal gain | LibraSpec, [2608.08721](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08721) |
| expert activation cost | EcoSpec, [2607.12696](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12696) |
| step-wise efficiency (entropy-controlled length) | SparseSpec-L, [2607.27735](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27735) |
| learned verification payoff | Hybrid Verified Decoding, [2606.01019](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01019) |

Two of those papers converge on the same criterion. SparseSpec-L states it
directly: *"extending the speculation horizon can reduce rather than improve
speedup when the marginal acceptance probability falls below the relative
drafting cost."*

I am not asking for any of them to be adopted. I am asking whether the K
decision should keep being a batch-keyed array index, given that the next six
proposals all need it not to be.

### Evidence I can offer, with its limits.

I ran the (batch, ctx) case, so the numbers below are about that one signal.
Full provenance, including what I have withdrawn, is in a
[ledger](https://github.com/seongyun1104/depthchart/blob/931ff25/EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md);
the per-cell working is in a
[companion note](https://github.com/seongyun1104/depthchart/blob/931ff25/POLICY_INTERFACE.md).

**1. The win localises to a single cell.** Position-balanced 2 trials, cache
wiped per launch, cold-start burn, 3 warm-up discarded + 3 measured per cell,
c=256, per-arm stdev at most 1.72 %, Gemma-4-31B-it-QAT-FP8 with its assistant
drafter on one H100 NVL. A batch-only schedule `[[1,64,3],[65,128,1],[129,512,0]]`
against a (bs, ctx) schedule that differs from it in exactly one cell — at
bs ≥ 129 and ctx ≥ 769, K=3 instead of K=0:

| ctx | batch-only | (bs, ctx) | ratio |
|---:|---:|---:|:-:|
| 400 | 1875.6 | 1890.7 | 1.01× |
| 900 | 1453.5 | 1874.6 | 1.29× |
| 1900 | 1416.6 | 1848.2 | 1.30× |
| 4000 | 1232.8 | 1680.4 | 1.36× |

The ctx=400 tie is the design working: there both schedules select K=0. The
mechanism is narrow and worth stating plainly — **at high batch a batch-only
schedule has to turn speculation off, and context is what tells you when to turn
it back on.**

The distinct-K set is `{0, 1, 3}` for both schedules, so this costs no extra
CUDA graphs; graphs are keyed on K, and the K values are the same ones.

**2. A cost model over the same interface gets that cell wrong.** I also have a
producer that derives the schedule from a stated cost model rather than typing
it — `K* = argmax_K E_accept(K) / (F(ctx) + K·M(bs))`, the same marginal-utility
shape LibraSpec and SparseSpec-L arrive at. Run with the coefficients it ships,
sweeping only the acceptance prior across 0.35–0.75 (the campaign observed
44–47 % in the K=3 tier), it selects **K=0 at the high-batch tier at every
context**. It reproduces the batch-only schedule and would not have found the
cell worth 29–36 %.

That gap closes under recalibration — the per-context coefficient has to be
roughly an order of magnitude larger relative to the per-batch one — not under a
change of functional form. I am reporting it because it is the honest state of
that producer: a stated model, uncalibrated, currently disagreeing with my own
measurement.

**3. What I have not established.** One model pair, one hardware configuration,
one concurrency, four context points, one differing cell. I have not calibrated
the cost model on hardware. I have not attributed the DSD baseline tax to its
terms — the 2×2 design for that is written and unrun. And the sharpness of the K
optimum at low batch did not clear its own pre-registered bar (#48627, and see
the ledger); the result above is at c=256, which is a different regime.

### Proposed Change.

**None yet — this asks for a decision, not a design.** I have a stake here
(#48944 is the ctx-axis version) and I would rather the shape be agreed before
more signals arrive than argue for mine.

The question is where the K decision should live:

1. **Keep it batch-keyed** and let each new signal negotiate its own widening.
   Predictable, and the dense array stays trivially cheap. #50488 has just made
   this the assumption in two more places, so this is the status quo by default
   rather than by decision.
2. **Let the schedule declare its own key set**, so `(bs, ctx)` and any later
   key are the same kind of object to the consumers. This is what #48944 does
   for one extra key; generalising it is a small change to the validator, the
   lookup and the three read sites.
3. **Separate the decision from the schedule**, so that a table, a cost model,
   or a runtime controller are interchangeable producers of K. Two producers
   already exist behind one schedule in my branch, which is the minimum evidence
   for this being more than speculative generality — but two is also the
   minimum, and I would not argue for it on that basis alone.

What I think matters more than which option: **nothing in the engine currently
measures the quantity these policies need.** Acceptance is exported in aggregate,
but per-`(batch bucket, ctx bucket, K)` draft and verify latency, first-rejection
position, committed tokens per verification, and K-keyed graph hit/miss are not.
My cost model missed the cell above because its coefficients were guesses; there
is no way to stop them being guesses from inside vLLM today. If only one thing
comes out of this thread, that telemetry is the one I would pick, and it is
independent of which option above wins.

I have opened #54748 for the smallest piece of it, so this is not a request for
someone else to do the work: steps the schedule sends to K=0 build no
`SpecDecodingStats` at all, so a schedule that has correctly stopped speculating
under load is indistinguishable from speculative decoding not running. That PR
adds a step counter keyed on the selected K and is deliberately independent of
everything proposed here.

### Feedback Period.

No deadline. I will not open a PR against any of the three options without
agreement here first.

### Any Other Things.

Related: RFC #48627 (the ctx axis specifically, with its evidence section
corrected on 2026-09-01), PR #48944, #54082, #49986, #49548, #48494.

Prior art on the ctx dependence itself: MagicDec
([blog](https://infini-ai-lab.github.io/MagicDec-part1/), paper
[2408.11049](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11049)) proposes choosing speculation
amount as a function of sequence length; TurboSpec/SmartSpec
([2406.14066](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14066)) is the batch-adaptive
predecessor of the schedule API this RFC is about.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary With `speculative-config {"method":"ngram"}` on a hybrid GDN/Mamba model, the XPU `gdn_attention` kernel asserts and the engine dies. The kernel requires a **uniform** speculative draft length across the batch; ngram produces a **ragged** one, because a partial n-gram match drafts fewer tokens than `num_speculative_tokens`. This is **not** the mixed prefill+decode batch case and **not** the empty-draft case. It reproduces with a single stream. ### Error ``` File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/_xpu_ops.py", line 171, in _gdn_attention_core_xpu_impl torch.ops._xpu_C.gdn_attention( RuntimeError: Expected spec_token == num_spec_decodes * (num_speculative_tokens + 1) to be true, but got false. ``` Reached via `qwen3_5.py:591 forward` → `qwen3_next.py:627 forward` → the AOT-compiled submodule → `_xpu_C.gdn_attention`. The engine does not recover: ``` EngineCore encountered a fatal error XPUWorker shutdown: cleaning up (rank=0, local_rank=0) vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError POST /v1/chat/completions -> 500 Application shutdown complete ``` ### Reproduction ```bash vllm serve /models/Qwen3.8-27B-GPTQ-Int4 \ --quantization gptq --dtype float16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-model-len 224000 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":3,"prompt_lookup_min":3,"prompt_lookup_max":3}' ``` Then send ordinary generation requests over semi-repetitive text (code, config files, anything the drafter can partially match). The crash arrives within a few hundred generated tokens. **`--max-num-seqs 1` is deliberate.** The engine log at the moment of the crash shows `Running: 1 reqs`, so batching is not required to trigger it and limiting concurrency does not avoid it. ### Drafter state immediately before the crash ``` Mean acceptance length: 1.74 Accepted: 32 tokens · Drafted: 129 tokens Per-position acceptance rate: 0.395, 0.233, 0.116 Avg Draft acceptance rate: 24.8% ``` The falling per-position rate is the point: drafts routinely die part-way through, which is exactly the ragged-length condition. ### Why the input distribution matters (and how to get a false negative) We initially failed to reproduce this with a synthetic probe and briefly concluded the bug was gone. The probe used random-word prompts, which give the drafter either **no** match (drafts 0 → no speculative batch → harmless) or a **full** match (drafts exactly N → equality holds). Only a **partial** match produces a draft of length 1 or 2, which is what breaks the equality. So a reproduction attempt needs content the drafter can *partially* match. Random tokens will pass and prove nothing. ### Why this is distinct from the existing issues - **#53077** (merged 2026-08-20) resets `num_spec_decodes` when *every* scheduled draft count is zero. Our build contains it and still asserts — this is the ragged case inside a *non-empty* schedule, not the all-zero case. - **#38196** / **#36917** / **#36918** are mixed decode + spec_decode *batch* problems. This reproduces at `Running: 1 reqs`. - **#53051** is a prefill misdispatched into the spec-decode cudagraph, a different mechanism with a different symptom (silent bad output, not an assert). - **#53928** is the `causal_conv1d` mixed prefill+decode error, fixed in vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.14.1 — this build has that fix. ### Notes - `prompt_lookup_min == prompt_lookup_max` does **not** avoid it. Those bound the match length searched, not the drafter's ability to emit a shorter draft (or none) when no match of that length exists. - `suffix` should fail identically, being variable-length by the same nature. - MTP is unaffected, since it always drafts exactly `num_speculative_tokens`. - Consequence on XPU: **MTP is the only usable speculation method for this model family**, and MTP is the one that interacts badly with prefix caching (see #50897 / #52244 / #53479). ### Suggested direction Either pad ragged speculative batches to a uniform draft length before the kernel call, or relax the kernel's equality to accept a per-request draft-length vector. The all-zero case already has precedent in #53077; this is the same class of problem one step further along. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next generates corrupted Thai orthography under vLLM; the same model under llama.cpp at the same QSA budget is clean
items.body:
### Summary

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` under vLLM produces systematically malformed Thai: single-character substitutions, displaced tone marks and doubled combining marks. The same model at the same effective QSA budget under llama.cpp is clean — 0 defects across 130 samples versus 12–18 per 1000 Thai characters across five vLLM configurations.

This was originally reported as part of #54521 (non-determinism from `persistent_topk`). It is a **separate defect**: I have since shown non-determinism is not its cause, and that QSA block selection is not either. Splitting it out so #54521 can stay scoped to determinism.

### Environment

- 2x DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121), `-tp 2`, aarch64, driver 580.159.03 / 580.95.05
- vLLM `0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198` (official `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next` body)
- `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, `--enforce-eager`, stock `indexer_budget=2048`
- Sampling: the model card's temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20. **Greedy is not usable for a quality measurement on this model** — it degenerates even at 105 prompt tokens — so every number below is a rate over 10 samples.

### What the corruption looks like

The probe is a Thai date-countdown answer, so the same words recur with unambiguous correct forms:

| correct | observed |
|---|---|
| `ปีใหม่` | `ปีใหม้` (mai tho for mai ek) |
| `สงกรานต์` | `สงกรานตค์์`, thanthakhat detached or missing |
| `ครับ` | `ครรับ` (doubled ro rua) |
| `คริสต์ศักราช` | `คริศต์ศักราช` (so sala for so suea) |
| `เช่น` | `เชน่` (tone mark displaced past the consonant) |
| `คำนวณ` | `คานวณ` (sara am lost) |
| `อีก` | `อีีก` (doubled sara ii) |

Thai is a sensitive detector rather than a special case: it runs ~3x more tokens per character than English, with many near-identical combining-mark tokens, so a perturbation surfaces as visibly broken text instead of a harmless paraphrase.

### Evidence

Prompt-length ladder built from a real captured agent request by dropping tool definitions and truncating the system prompt; the conversation itself is never touched, so every rung asks the identical question. N=10 per cell, corrupt / informative samples:

| prompt tok | 20394 | 16006 | 13369 | 9635 | 8556 | 6490 | 4675 | 2959 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM stock | 6/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 | 9/9 | 9/10 | 10/10 | 7/9 | 7/10 |
| vLLM, no MTP | 7/10 | 7/10 | 7/10 | 9/9 | 7/10 | 6/8 | 6/9 | 6/8 |
| **llama.cpp** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** |

Five further rungs from 2631 down to 1720 tokens: vLLM 6–10/10, llama.cpp 0/10. **The corruption is not length-gated.**

A structural detector (stacked tone marks, doubled upper vowels, tone-then-vowel — independent of the word list above) over every sample collected:

| engine / configuration | samples | Thai chars | defects per 1k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| vLLM stock | 77 | 5981 | 16.55 |
| vLLM stock, short rungs | 113 | 9316 | 15.99 |
| vLLM without the sort patch | 78 | 6751 | 17.63 |
| vLLM `indexer_budget=8192` | 77 | 6486 | 14.96 |
| vLLM without MTP | 76 | 5737 | 12.90 |
| **llama.cpp UD-IQ4_XS** | **130** | **11085** | **0.00** |

### The llama.cpp comparison is matched, not approximate

llama.cpp build 10731, `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` UD-IQ4_XS, single GB10, `--jinja -c 32768`. It implements QSA itself and does not fall back to dense attention:

- `src/models/qwen4exp.cpp:423` — "QSA attends to a budget of whole blocks of compress_ratio tokens, plus the incomplete tail; one mean-pooled indexer key scores each block"
- `build_qsa_top_k` → `ggml_top_k(ctx0, expanded, width)` with `width = min(n_kv, indexer_top_k + r - 1)`, then the KQ mask is unmasked only at the selected cells

At the 20k rung that is **2051 attended tokens of 20343**. vLLM at stock `indexer_budget=2048` attends `k=512` blocks × `compress_ratio=4` = **2048 tokens**. Same algorithm, same budget, same ~10:1 sparsity, from GGUF metadata that is the model's own (`indexer.top_k = 2048`, `compress_ratios = [0,0,0,4,...]`, `full_attention_interval = 4`).

### Ruled out

- **QSA sparse block selection.** Density is `prompt_tokens <= indexer_budget` (the compress ratio cancels), so shortening the prompt reaches genuinely dense selection. Five dense cells — 4/8, 7/10, 9/10, 6/10, 8/10 — all corrupt at the sparse rate. Dense selection does not help.
- **Non-determinism.** A deterministic tie-break makes the real payload byte-identical across runs and leaves the Thai just as corrupt (#54521).
- **Speculative decoding.** `--speculative-config` removed: still 6–9/10 corrupt, 12.90 defects per 1k.
- **Quantization.** UD-IQ4_XS is a *coarser* quant than the FP8 used under vLLM, and the lower-precision weights are the clean ones.
- **The weights / the model / the QSA algorithm.** Clean under llama.cpp.
- Also eliminated earlier in #54521: prefix caching, chat template, `rows_per_chunk`, #53287, CUDA graphs (`--enforce-eager` throughout), the weight loader, and `indexer_budget` overrides.

### Not controlled

Two differences between the engines remain uncontrolled, and I would rather state them than argue them away.

**1. Chat template.** llama.cpp used the GGUF's built-in template; vLLM used a locally fixed jinja template. Prompt lengths differ by ~50 tokens per rung. The chat template was independently eliminated as a cause earlier in #54521, but it was not held identical across this particular comparison.

**2. Tensor parallelism.** llama.cpp ran single-GPU; vLLM ran `-tp 2`. I cannot close this on my hardware — FP8 is ~193 GiB (96.5 GiB per rank) and NVFP4 is 125.9 GiB, both above one GB10's ~121 GiB, so no vLLM variant of this model runs at `-tp 1` here.

**This is the most useful thing someone else could check:** does the Thai corruption reproduce on a single large-memory GPU at `-tp 1`, and on non-GB10 hardware? That would separate a tensor-parallel bug from something in the `qwen4exp` implementation generally.

### Reproduction

Any Thai generation task shows it; a short factual answer in Thai is enough, and it reproduces from 1720 tokens of prompt upward. Score with a stacked-mark detector (tone+tone, upper+upper, tone-then-vowel adjacency) rather than by eye — but note that detector is a **lower bound**, since it does not catch the substitution errors, which are the majority. Harness and all raw samples available on request.

items.title: [Bug]: `--load-format dummy` OOMs on large FP8 parameters — `initialize_single_dummy_weight` materializes a full-size fp16 temporary
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
GPUs      : 8x NVIDIA CMP 170HX (GA100, compute capability 8.0, 64 GB each),
            driver 610.43.02
vLLM      : 0.28.1rc1.dev132+ge126687a9  (main @ e126687a, source build)
PyTorch   : 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12
Model     : Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (fused PLE table = 47.7 GiB in FP8)
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py:1360` (`initialize_single_dummy_weight`):

```python
if torch.finfo(param.data.dtype).bits < 16:
    # uniform_ doesn't support < 16-bit datatypes (FP8)
    dtype = param.data.dtype
    tmp_param = param.data.to(torch.float16)
    tmp_param = tmp_param.uniform_(low, high, generator=generator).to(dtype)
    param.data.copy_(tmp_param)
```

`param.data.to(torch.float16)` allocates a temporary **twice the size of the parameter**, plus a
second same-size temporary for the `.to(dtype)` result. For a 47.7 GiB FP8 tensor — the fused PLE
embedding table of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — that is ~95 GiB of scratch on top of the 47.7 GiB already
resident, so it OOMs on any single GPU regardless of how the model itself is sharded.

The practical consequence: `--load-format dummy`, which is the standard way to validate a
parallelism/partition configuration without waiting on weight I/O, is unusable for exactly the
models where that validation is most expensive to get wrong.

### Suggested fix

Initialize in chunks when the parameter is large and contiguous; peak scratch becomes a fixed
~128 MiB (64 Mi elements at fp16) instead of 2x the parameter:

```python
if torch.finfo(param.data.dtype).bits < 16:
    dtype = param.data.dtype
    step = 64 * 1024 * 1024
    if param.data.numel() > step and param.data.is_contiguous():
        flat = param.data.view(-1)
        for i in range(0, flat.numel(), step):
            sl = flat[i : i + step]
            tmp = sl.to(torch.float16)
            tmp = tmp.uniform_(low, high, generator=generator).to(dtype)
            sl.copy_(tmp)
    else:
        tmp_param = param.data.to(torch.float16)
        tmp_param = tmp_param.uniform_(low, high, generator=generator).to(dtype)
        param.data.copy_(tmp_param)
```

This lowers peak memory for every FP8 model under dummy load, not just the huge-embedding case.
(The generated values differ from the single-shot path only in how the generator stream is
consumed, which is irrelevant for dummy weights.)

With this change, `--load-format dummy` on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 completes and the PP partition
can be validated in minutes instead of loading 173 GB of real weights.

Happy to send this as a PR.

*AI assistance was used to diagnose this and to draft the report; the failure and the fix were
both reproduced on the hardware described.*

items.title: [RFC]: fp8 KV cache support for Inkling on SM100-family GPUs
items.body:
### Motivation.

Inkling and Inkling-Small serve with a bf16 KV cache only. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` fails at JIT warmup: the cache is allocated as uint8, nothing in the Inkling stack reinterprets it as an fp8 dtype, and both kernel backends assert on the dtype.

KV memory is the binding constraint for long context on memory-limited deployments. fp8 halves attention KV bytes across the stack (7,168 to 3,584 bytes/token/rank at TP4: the 7 full-attention layers at 1,024 bytes/token/layer; the 35 sliding-window layers hold only their 512-token window, so they do not scale with context). The realized pool gain depends on serving settings, because the per-request pool charge is dominated by the bf16-pinned conv-state admission reserve, which this change cannot touch. Measured through vLLM's own `get_kv_cache_configs` at the same memory budget:

| max_model_len | max_num_batched_tokens | pool gain (fp8 vs bf16) |
|---|---|---|
| 8,192 | 16,384 | +5.9% |
| 131,072 | 16,384 (serve default) | +8.6% |
| 131,072 | 2,048 | +28.1% |
| 1,048,576 | 16,384 | +27.9% |
| 1,048,576 | 2,048 | +73.1% |

The 1M configuration was validated live, not just modeled: two servers booted at max_model_len 1,048,576 measured +73.06% pool capacity against the +73.1% prediction, with capacity for 24 concurrent 1M-token requests under fp8 vs 14 under bf16 (vLLM's logged maximum concurrency), and cold-prefill TTFT at 0.84x bf16 at 1M. Kernel-level attention speedups reach 1.45x and grow with KV length.

### Proposed Change.

Two PRs, sequenced. The kernel PR merges first; the wiring PR references it; a follow-up bumps the vendored pin.

1. tml-fa4 kernel PR (vllm-project/tml-fa4#4): plain per-tensor fp8 e4m3 Q/KV support in the Blackwell sheared-bias forward kernel. 4 files, +148/-27, based on current main (b206834, the exact commit vLLM vendors). It adapts closed PR vllm-project/tml-fa4#1 and fixes a correctness bug in it: with fp8 P pre-scaled by 2\*\*8, the lazy-rescale slack that guarantees zero P clipping is log2(448) - 8 = 0.807, but that PR set rescale_threshold=4.0. Attention bias makes sub-threshold row-max jumps routine, clipping P (six deterministic test failures, 0.3-0.7 abs error, root cause proven by zero-bias diagnostic and three-arm bisection: threshold=0 fixes, max_offset=0 fixes, ex2-tuning-off does not). We ship rescale_threshold=0.75, chosen to guarantee the invariant with margin for compiler reassociation. The empirical failure onset sits between 1.5 and 2.0 with monotonic dose-response beyond it.

2. vLLM wiring PR: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` for Inkling. 8 files, +596/-35 across two commits (the feature, plus a clean NotImplementedError for quantized KV dtypes on the ROCm path; non-test delta ~260 lines). Runtime-validated on v0.28.0; cherry-picks cleanly onto main as of 2026-08-28 (4c6c9d5).

3. Follow-up after (1) merges: bump the tml-fa4 GIT_TAG in cmake/external_projects/tml_fa4.cmake.

Design summary:

- Quant-on-store. K/V are already computed in fp32 inside the fused qkvr_prep store kernels; with fp8 active they are multiplied by the reciprocal scale, clamped to the e4m3 finite range (+/-448), and stored as e4m3. Write-path cost is -1.3% to +2.0% vs the bf16 store (median ratio 1.01); the added multiply+clamp+convert is offset by halved write bytes.
- Scales. Per-tensor, per-layer k_scale/v_scale, default 1.0, loaded from checkpoint tensors `model.llm.layers.<i>.attn.{k,v}_scale` through the standard loader path with no flags. Q is quantized with a static per-tensor scale after qkvr_prep.
- Kernel read path. The shipped sheared kernel takes fp8 Q/KV directly and adds no descale parameters; both descales are per-tensor scalars applied at the vLLM wrapper (fa4_rel_attention.py). The QK descale is folded into softmax_scale, so scores are descaled before the relative position bias is added and the bias term stays exact; the V descale is applied as a post-hoc multiply on the kernel output, which is linear in V. The fold sits outside the backend branch and is path-independent: the CuTe score-mod fallback receives the same folded softmax_scale and output multiply, since neither vendored varlen entry exposes descale parameters.
- Gating. SM100-family e4m3 only; a clear error is raised elsewhere. ROCm gains no fp8 path: quantized KV dtypes are rejected at layer construction (second wiring commit); non-quantized dtypes are untouched.
- Conv state stays bf16. It is pinned to model dtype, unaffected by kv_cache_dtype; conv-cache stores are untouched and verified bit-identical to the bf16 run.
- Load-time warning. If fp8 KV is enabled and the checkpoint carries v_scale tensors for fewer layers than run quantized (coverage-checked at model level from the loader's return value, since unity values are legitimate in a calibrated checkpoint), a warning names the measured failure mode; loaded scales are validated finite and positive.
- CI. New tests live under tests/models/inkling/ and are picked up by the existing B200 Inkling Buildkite entry (key inkling-unit-tests-b200); no CI config change.

### Evidence Summary

Serving measurements on B200 (SM100), vLLM v0.28.0, TP4, two identical 4-GPU servers (bf16 vs fp8), greedy, paired prompts. Kernel-level numbers are from a separate single-B200 host. The full evidence document with per-run artifacts and the pre-registered gate scorecard will be attached to the wiring PR.

| axis | result |
|---|---|
| kernel correctness | 160/160 tests across the three test files this change touches: both backends, fp8 x {sheared, scoremod} x scale sets x rel extents, atol/rtol 0.15 vs a dequantized-input fp32 reference, plus spec/warmup/gate tests |
| kernel latency | fp8 faster in 18/20 cases; best 1.45x (batched decode, kv=64K, b=32); worst regression +2.6% |
| long-context logprobs (book-length docs, longest 121K scored tokens, noise-free paired design, production path) | on the stable documents (5/10; the replication-unstable documents, four high-PPL and one at PPL 14, are excluded from certification because they amplify replication noise, see evidence doc), every position bucket within +/-0.71% PPL on both fp8 configs; deepest bucket (64K-128K) ~0.1%; median across all 10 docs +0.21% (unity) / +0.16% (calibrated); top-1 agreement rises with depth; no error compounding |
| GSM8K / MMLU (n=14,042) / IFEval / HumanEval | parity on all four on the score-mod path, paired McNemar per sample; GSM8K and MMLU repeated at parity on the production sheared path |
| tool calling, 500-call replay | 475 vs 474 pass, McNemar p=1.0; 100% JSON- and schema-valid on both arms; 50/50 negatives correctly silent |
| needle-in-a-haystack (custom paired single-needle test, substituted for the pre-registered RULER suite; no multi-needle or aggregation coverage) | 120/120 both dtypes to 120K; at the 1M boot, 27/27 paired retrievals including needles ~950K tokens behind the query |
| capacity, live 1M boot | +73.06% measured vs +73.1% predicted; 24 vs 14 concurrent 1M-token requests |
| TTFT, cold single request | 0.96x at 256K, 0.91x at 512K, 0.84x at 1M (fp8 faster, monotonic in context) |
| serving throughput | parity within +/-1.1% up to 32K contexts; +2.2% total tok/s and -2.3% TTFT at 100K prefill; two exceptions: decode-workload median TTFT +10.2% (143.7 to 158.3 ms, p99 improves) and mid-workload median TTFT +2.7% |

Known limitation: MATH-500 regresses at unity scale.

- -4.2pt mean (41.9 to 37.7, triplicate runs per arm, run-level p 0.05-0.10; direction consistent across all 9 cross-run pairings). Every other task in the battery is at parity.
- Mechanism, measured: V outliers clip at unity scale, concentrated in the global attention layers (max |V| = 1,272 vs e4m3 max 448; the worst global layer clips ~1 in 1,100 V elements). K never clips anywhere. Global layers carry long-range information, consistent with the deficit surfacing only on long-derivation math.
- Remedy: calibrated v_scale recovers about half the deficit (37.7 to 39.7 mean; the best calibrated run, 41.0, comes within 0.8pt of the weakest bf16 run at 41.8, while the best unity run reaches only 39.4) at no cost elsewhere (GSM8K 83.55% on the calibrated server, center of the healthy band). Per-layer calibration of this checkpoint touches 14 of 42 layers, all v_scale, no k_scale.
- The wiring PR ships the coverage-checked warning. A standalone calibration utility exists: it hooks the fused store sites, measures real per-layer K/V ranges, derives clip-free per-layer scales, and writes them into the checkpoint for the existing loader. llm-compressor cannot calibrate this model because its HF-side observers never see Inkling's post-norm/post-conv fused store sites.

### Related Finding

The conv-state admission reserve that mutes the capacity gain at serve defaults is a separate, dtype-independent accounting behavior: tiny-window SlidingWindowSpec conv state is charged a per-request in-flight reserve that reaches 84% of per-request blocks. It affects any KV compression on hybrid conv models, not just this change. Filed separately as vllm-project/vllm#54703; it is referenced here to explain the sensitivity table above.

### Feedback Requested

1. Calibration tool placement. The documented KV-scale pathway is out-of-tree calibration via llm-compressor, which cannot observe this model's fused store sites (K is stored post-rms-norm and post-conv inside a fused kernel). Our prepared default: keep the utility out-of-tree and add a short Inkling section to docs/features/quantization/quantized_kvcache.md (drafted, ready to include). Alternatives if preferred: land it under examples/, or upstream the flow into llm-compressor as the long-term home.
2. Unity-scale serving behavior. Given the measured MATH-500 regression at unity scale, should serving an fp8 KV checkpoint without v_scale tensors warn (current behavior) or refuse unless explicitly opted in? The warning matches the existing unity-scale warning convention in BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading; we kept that precedent and would want a strong reason to diverge from it for one model.
3. ROCm scope. This proposal gates fp8 KV to SM100-family e4m3; the ROCm path rejects quantized KV dtypes at layer construction with an explicit NotImplementedError (included in the wiring PR, with a CPU test). A tracking issue for ROCm parity is drafted and ready to file if wanted.
4. Checkpoint scale schema. The emitted tensor names are in vLLM's canonical post-remap form and an opt-in flag records kv_cache_quant_algo=FP8 so kv_cache_dtype="auto" resolves to fp8 for downstream consumers. Any objection to that convention for this model?

### Feedback Period.

At least one week. Two weeks preferred: reproducing the end-to-end evidence requires B200 hardware.

### CC List.

Quantization: @mgoin @robertgshaw2-redhat @tlrmchlsmth @yewentao256 @pavanimajety @zyongye. Attention: @LucasWilkinson @MatthewBonanni. Inkling: @mikekg. @WoosukKwon authored vllm-project/tml-fa4#1, which the kernel PR adapts.

### Any Other Things.

- AI assistance disclosure: AI was used to implement, benchmark, debug, and document this work. The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and can explain and defend the implementation. Commits carry Co-authored-by trailers alongside Signed-off-by, per the contributing guide.
- Per the contributing guide's threshold, this RFC is optional (the wiring PR's non-test delta is ~260 lines); it is posted alongside the PRs (the wiring PR stays in draft) to collect design feedback, primarily on the questions above.
- Two pre-registered gates failed as written and are disclosed in the evidence document's scorecard. The top-1 agreement gate (>=99% short / >=97% long) was ill-posed: the bf16-vs-bf16 control arm itself scores 88.2-90.5% under prefix perturbation, and fp8 agreement is within ~1pt of that control in every bucket. The zero-KV-clip-at-unity gate failed on V (pooled 2.2e-5; K exact 0): this is the V-clipping mechanism behind the MATH-500 deficit described above. The scorecard also records that RULER was replaced by the custom paired single-needle NIAH noted in the evidence table, and the canonical-evaluator GSM8K cross-check was not run (its pre-registered bound is a <=1.0pt delta; within-harness deltas: 0.83pt on the sheared path, inside that bound; 1.82pt on the score-mod path, outside it, fp8-favored).
