items.title: [Bug]: EngineCore hangs indefinitely in torch.xpu.graphs.replay() under concurrent load on Intel Arc B70 (Battlemage)
items.body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM version: 0.27.2rc1.dev77+gac7509e2b
torch: 2.13.0+xpu
GPU: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics (Battlemage), single device
Backend: native torch XPU (no IPEX installed)
Model: Qwen3-30B-A3B-class model, GPTQ Int4, served as "qwen38"
Launch flags (relevant):
  vllm serve /model --quantization gptq --dtype float16 \
    --max-model-len 110000 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 9216 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-log-requests
  (speculative decoding / MTP toggled via an env var wrapper around vllm serve;
   both MTP-on and MTP-off configurations reproduce this issue)
```

### Model Input Dumps

Not applicable — this is a hang, not a crash/incorrect-output bug, so there is no failing request payload to attach. Happy to capture one if it would help.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Under sustained concurrent load (2 agentic API clients issuing overlapping long-running
chat completions against the same server), the vLLM EngineCore process periodically
enters a genuine infinite spin inside `torch.xpu.graphs.replay()` (the CUDA/XPU-graph
replay call), pegging one CPU core at 100% and never returning. The server stops
responding to new requests; from the outside this looks like a hang, and our
`llama-swap`-based reverse proxy eventually kills and restarts the whole backend
service after its health probe (a real inference call) itself gets stuck behind the
spin.

This has recurred roughly every 10–25 minutes of concurrent-load runtime over
multiple independent sessions on this box, on both an MTP-enabled and an MTP-disabled
configuration, and is not correlated with `vllm:num_preemptions_total` (confirmed 0 at
the moment of at least one capture) or KV-cache eviction — i.e. it is not simply
"ran out of KV cache and got stuck recovering." It occurs while other engine threads
are otherwise idle (`Thread-1`/`Thread-2` housekeeping threads shown idle in every
capture below).

We confirmed this is a genuine spin, not a slow-but-progressing call, by taking
repeated `py-spy dump` snapshots of the same EngineCore PID several seconds apart:
the captured Python frame is byte-identical across snapshots, and `/proc/<pid>/stat`
cumulative CPU ticks climb steadily between snapshots (e.g. one PID: 55960 → 124899 →
263597 → 293561 ticks across four captures ~10–70 min apart, same top frame every time).

**Two distinct stack-trace variants of the same underlying `replay()` spin have been
observed** on this box, depending on whether speculative decoding (MTP) is enabled:

**Variant A — via the MTP/speculative-decode draft-proposal path:**
```
Thread (active): "MainThread"
    replay (torch/xpu/graphs.py:107)
    __call__ (vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py:360)
    execution_fn (<string>:10)
    __call__ (vllm/compilation/caching.py:225)
    forward (vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py:284)
    __call__ (torch/_dynamo/aot_compile.py:244)
    __call__ (vllm/compilation/decorators.py:520)
    propose (vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py:755)
    propose_draft_token_ids (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:5366)
    propose_draft_token_ids (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:4718)
```

**Variant B — via the regular (non-speculative) decode forward path, observed after
disabling MTP as a mitigation attempt:**
```
Thread (active): "MainThread"
    replay (torch/xpu/graphs.py:107)
    __call__ (vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py:360)
    _model_forward (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:3970)
    execute_model (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:4554)
    decorate_context (torch/utils/_contextlib.py:124)
    execute_model (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:1086)
    decorate_context (torch/utils/_contextlib.py:124)
    execute_model (vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py:351)
    run_method (vllm/v1/serial_utils.py:510)
    collective_rpc (vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py:109)
```

Both bottom out at the identical frame: `replay (torch/xpu/graphs.py:107)` called from
`vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py:360`. This strongly suggests the bug is in the XPU
graph-replay call itself (or the state it depends on), not in either calling path —
MTP just changes which code path reaches it first/more often.

**Mitigation tried:** disabling MTP (speculative decoding) reduces frequency and
appears to make the spin less likely to require a full service restart to recover
from, and improves realized end-to-end throughput under concurrent load (measured
~44% higher tokens/sec over a wall-clock window, accounting for outage time), but does
**not** eliminate the spin — Variant B above was captured with MTP fully disabled.

**Independent third-party corroboration:** a public benchmarking log for the same
GPU (`steveseguin/b70-optimization-lab`, README) documents XPU-graph + MTP
producing corrupted/zero-acceptance output on this hardware generation:
> `MTP1 + XPU graph | 7.63 tok/s | 0.00 acceptance | corrupt (0/25) - do not use`
> `MTP off, XPU graph on (two boots) | 30.22 / 30.26 tok/s | - | faithful (23/25, within boot envelope)`

That log documents output corruption specifically with MTP+graph, which is a
different symptom (wrong output vs. our hang) but points at the same suspect
component (XPU graph replay interacting with speculative decoding) on the same GPU
family, and independently supports MTP+graph being unreliable on Battlemage.

Related-but-not-identical issues we found and ruled out as duplicates:
- vllm-project/vllm#48327 — same class of Intel-XPU CUDA-graph-replay issue, but
  reported as producing garbage output, not a hang.
- pytorch/pytorch#187277 — XPU graph replay crash (not a spin) on similar hardware.

Neither exactly matches a genuine infinite spin with climbing CPU and no crash/error,
so filing this as a distinct report rather than a duplicate.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Serve a GPTQ-quantized model on a single Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage) via vLLM's
   native XPU backend, with CUDA/XPU graph capture enabled (default), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.
2. Drive sustained concurrent load: 2+ long-running agentic/chat-completion clients
   issuing overlapping requests continuously for tens of minutes.
3. Periodically (observed every ~10–25 min of concurrent runtime), the EngineCore
   process's MainThread enters `torch.xpu.graphs.replay()` and never returns; CPU
   usage for that thread pegs at 100% indefinitely. Confirm via repeated `py-spy dump`
   of the EngineCore PID showing an identical frame with climbing `/proc/<pid>/stat`
   CPU ticks across snapshots taken minutes apart.
4. The server stops answering any new request; recovery currently requires a full
   process restart (nothing short of restart has been found to un-stick it).

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: Speculative kv_cache_dtype=fp8 crashes startup on hybrid GDN models - FlashInfer "Unrecognized dtype: auto", then native crash on SM89 with explicit target dtype
items.body:
### Summary Setting a **draft-only** KV cache dtype via `--speculative-config '{"kv_cache_dtype": "fp8", ...}'` on a hybrid GDN model (Qwen3.5-family: full-attention + GDN layers) crashes engine startup in the FlashInfer attention metadata builder: ``` ValueError: Unrecognized dtype: auto ``` The identical launch **without** the speculative `kv_cache_dtype` field works fine (bf16 KV everywhere). Explicitly setting `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` on the target (so no group carries the raw `auto`) gets past this error, but the engine then dies with a **native crash** (no Python traceback) during attention init on SM89. Checked against current `main`: both `LLMBaseProposer._create_draft_vllm_config()` (kv_cache_dtype passthrough) and `FlashInferBackend.get_dtype_for_flashinfer()` (no `auto` mapping) are unchanged, so this should still reproduce on main. ### Environment
collect-env (abridged)
vLLM 0.28.0 (pip wheel)
PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3, Ubuntu 24.04
4x RTX 4090 (SM89, PCIe), TP4, CUDA runtime 12.8
Attention backend: FlashInfer (auto-selected; the drafter needs non-causal attention)
Target: Qwen3.5-family hybrid model (full-attn + GDN layers), INT8-W8A16
Draft: DFlash2 drafter (method="dflash")
Full `vllm collect-env` output available on request.
### Reproduction ```bash vllm serve \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --max-model-len 200000 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": , "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "kv_cache_dtype": "fp8"}' ``` Any hybrid GDN target + draft-model-style speculative method should hit the same path; the draft does not need to be DFlash specifically. ### Actual behavior **Failure 1** - with only the speculative `"kv_cache_dtype": "fp8"`, every TP worker fails during `initialize_kv_cache`: ```python-traceback File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 680, in initialize_from_config self.model_runner.initialize_kv_cache(kv_cache_config) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 532, in initialize_kv_cache self.attn_groups, attn_cg_support, self.kernel_block_sizes = init_attn_backend(...) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 156, in init_attn_backend group.create_metadata_builders(...) File "vllm/v1/worker/utils.py", line 275, in create_metadata_builders builder_cls(...) File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py", line ~840, in FlashInferMetadataBuilder.__init__ self.kv_cache_dtype = FlashInferBackend.get_dtype_for_flashinfer(...) File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py", line 514, in get_dtype_for_flashinfer raise ValueError(f"Unrecognized dtype: {kv_cache_dtype}") ValueError: Unrecognized dtype: auto ``` `get_dtype_for_flashinfer()` only maps `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3`/`fp8_e5m2`/`nvfp4*`. In the normal single-dtype flow the raw `auto` is resolved to the model dtype before attention init; with a speculative `kv_cache_dtype` set, at least one attention group of the hybrid model appears to receive the **unresolved** string. Likely suspects: the GDN KV group, or the target-side group of the multi-group KV config created alongside the draft config. **Failure 2** - adding `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` (target) so no group carries `auto`: ``` ERROR [core.py:1346] EngineCore failed to start. ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:311] Worker proc VllmWorker-3 died unexpectedly (exit code: None) ``` i.e. a native crash of one worker during (draft) attention initialization on SM89, no Python traceback. The FlashInfer fp8-KV path appears to be non-functional on Ada for this (draft, non-causal) configuration, and it takes the whole engine down instead of failing backend selection with a readable error. ### Expected behavior Either: 1. draft KV cache dtype is honored (draft fp8, target bf16), or 2. startup fails fast with a clear error, e.g. "fp8 draft KV cache is not supported with backend FlashInfer on SM89", instead of `ValueError: Unrecognized dtype: auto` / silent worker native crash. ### Related issues - #48380 / PR #48381 - same family (draft inheriting a target-only KV dtype), but for MLA `fp8_ds_mla` layouts; this report is the draft-only `fp8` path on a hybrid GDN target. - #44184, #48406 - fp8 KV cache crashes together with spec decode. - #49077, #52202 - fp8 KV support work for pre-SM89 GPUs. - #54341 - fp8_e5m2/e4m3 KV writer mismatches. Happy to test patches / provide full logs.

items.title: [Perf]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 4xH800 TP4: v0.28.0 is ~3x slower TTFT and 21-41% lower throughput than v0.26.0 (measured with thinking disabled on both)
items.body:
> **Baseline figures corrected 2026-09-01** — the v0.26 conc=8 / conc=32 TTFT numbers first posted here (183 ms / 330 ms) were misquoted from a different run. Re-derived from the baseline CSV, they are **57 ms / 69 ms**, which makes the regression larger than originally stated (up to ~24× at conc=32), not smaller. All 0.28 figures are unchanged.

### Summary

Serving **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731** on 4×H800 (SM90, TP4), upgrading **v0.26.0 → v0.28.0** improves decode throughput (+8–21%) but regresses **first-token latency ~6–20×**. There appears to be a **constant ~1s/request prefill overhead** in 0.28 that exists even for ~16-token prompts at concurrency 1, persists in steady state (it is the *median* over hundreds of post-warmup requests, not a first-touch/compile artifact), and compounds into severe admission queueing at moderate concurrency. We swept every knob we could find (details below) and could not recover 0.26-class TTFT.

### Environment

- 4×H800 80GB (SM90), single node, TP=4
- Driver 580.173.02 / CUDA 13.0
- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0` official image (cu13 flavor), `--ipc=host --network host`
- Baseline: v0.26.0 (pip venv, torch cu129) on the same node, same weights, same flags
- Model: local `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (fp8), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, model-native max len (1M)
- Serve flags (both versions): `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-prompt-tokens-details` (variations noted per row)
- Load generator: async OpenAI-compat client, ~16-token prompts, 200–400 token outputs, temperature 0, concurrency 1 / 8 / 32
- Test order per config: one ~22k-token warmup request first, then single, then conc=8 (~80+ requests), then conc=32 (~100–300 requests) — so the conc=32 medians are measured on an engine that has already served 100+ requests
- All 0.28 runs use `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`. With the auto-enabled default (=1, which logs that it disables the torch.compile pipeline) we instead hit CUDA OOM: at init with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, or on the first ~22k-token prefill with 0.90. This matches the throughput findings in #49370, so the whole sweep was done with `=0`.

### Numbers (TTFT p50 per request; decode tok/s per stream)

| Config | single TTFT | conc=8 TTFT | conc=32 TTFT | conc=32 decode/stream |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **v0.26.0** (MRV1, 8192, util 0.90) | **48 ms** | **57 ms** | **69 ms** | 58.8 |
| v0.28.0, 8192, util 0.90, +kv-offloading 200GB | 681 ms | 1013 ms | **48.1 s** | (99.1, inflated by queueing) |
| v0.28.0, 8192, util 0.90 | n/a | 1188 ms | 7.10 s | 76.8 |
| v0.28.0, **16384**, util 0.85 (new default budget) | n/a | 1093 ms | **1.81 s** (best) | 63.4 |
| v0.28.0, MRV1 forced (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY, 8192, 0.90) | n/a | 1172 ms | 2.34 s | 56.7 |
| v0.28.0, 16384, 0.85, `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=4096` | n/a | 1254 ms | 2.16 s | 56.5 |
| v0.28.0, 16384, 0.85, `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` | n/a | 981 ms | **49.3 s** | **15.4 (collapse)** |
| v0.28.0, MRV1 forced + 16384 + 0.85 | — | — | — | engine core init failure |

Observations:

1. **A constant ~1s/request first-token cost is present in every 0.28 config**, including single-stream with ~16-token prompts (681 ms vs 48 ms on 0.26 — 14×). It is steady-state: conc=8 p50 sits at 1.0–1.2 s in *every* configuration across ~80 post-warmup requests (0.26 does 57 ms), and the single-stream case shows all three sequential requests equally slow, not just the first. It is also not a long-prompt chunking effect: raising `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` 512→4096 changed nothing, and the tiny-prompt case shows the overhead too.
2. Raising `--max-num-batched-tokens` to the new 16384 default (#51726) recovers most of the *queueing* (48 s → 1.8 s at conc=32) but the per-request floor remains ~1 s.
3. Forcing Model Runner V1 (allowed per #51768 with non-piecewise graphs) improves conc=32 TTFT ~3× vs MRV2 at the same flags (7.1 s → 2.3 s), but is still ~7× off 0.26, and fails engine-core init when combined with 16384 + util 0.85.
4. The default sparse backend (FlashMLA family) is the better of the two on SM90: forcing `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` collapses conc=32 decode to 15 tok/s with ~49 s TTFT.
5. Decode throughput is genuinely better on 0.28 in clean configs (single 149.8 → 174.9, conc=8 100.6 → 122.3, conc=32 58.6 → 63.4 tok/s) — the regression is specific to the prefill/first-token path.
6. KV offloading (`--kv-offloading-size 200`) works functionally on 0.28 (≈258 GB written through, no crashes — thanks for the post-0.26 fixes), but under load it amplifies the TTFT problem (48 s at conc=32), presumably from transfer contention.

### Suspicion

The per-request floor smells like the new sparse MLA prefill path that became the default for this model in 0.27/0.28. Possibly related: #54179 and #52339 (FlashMLA sparse prefill assertions on H20 — same kernel family, adjacent SM90 hardware), and #51430/#52401 (eager cudagraph region reshuffling for this model, which is also what forces MRV2 by default per #51768).

### Questions

1. Is a ~0.7–1.2 s per-request first-token floor for DSV4 on SM90 known/expected on 0.28, or a regression worth bisecting?
2. Is there a supported way to select the 0.26-era prefill path for this model on 0.28+, to keep the decode gains without the TTFT floor?

Happy to run additional experiments or bisect specific PRs on this hardware — the node and the harness that produced the table are still available.
